page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server instance configured with an AMD EPYC 9575F processor based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 20 virtual CPUs mapped to 20 physical cores with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.8 GB of RAM per core. Graphics and parallel computing acceleration are delivered by two NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined total of 96 GB of VRAM.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier performance in single-core processing, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and bzip3 single-threaded decompression. Multi-core performance is strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory performance is similarly robust, with read and write bandwidths consistently placing in the top 25%. For large language model inference, the server achieves top-tier speeds for prompt processing and text generation with a small 135M model, and strong text generation speeds with a medium 7B model.

A key architectural tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and the absence of local storage, meaning storage must be attached externally. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of GPU memory and system RAM relative to the 20 vCPUs makes it a specialized option for workloads requiring high-capacity VRAM without needing a massive physical CPU footprint. This configuration is suitable for machine learning inference, data science, image processing, and memory-intensive parallel computing tasks.
